claims.rule: Every intent has a title a person would say, not its type name.
claims.why: Siri tells intents apart by their titles, and Shortcuts lists them by title.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Read each action's `title` in the bundle's App Intents metadata; fail when it is empty or equals the intent's type name.
claims.fix: Give the intent `static let title: LocalizedStringResource = "<what it does, in a person's words>"`.

claims.rule: Every intent has a description that says what it does, beyond its title.
claims.why: Siri decides which intent fits a request from its title and description together.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Read each action's `descriptionMetadata.descriptionText`; fail when it is missing, empty or the same as the title.
claims.fix: Add `static let description = IntentDescription("<what it does and what it returns>")`.

claims.rule: Every parameter has a title.
claims.why: Siri and Shortcuts show the title when they ask the person for a value.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Read each parameter's `title` in the metadata; fail when it is empty.
claims.fix: Pass `title:` to the parameter's `@Parameter`.

claims.rule: Every parameter has a description that says what value it wants.
claims.why: Siri fills parameters from what the person said, guided by each parameter's description.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Read each parameter's `parameterDescription` in the metadata; fail when it is missing or empty.
claims.fix: Pass `description:` to `@Parameter`, saying what the value is and what form it takes.

claims.rule: The app's main actions are tool intents (`@AppIntent(.tool)`) or adopt a Siri schema, so Siri AI can call them.
claims.why: With the Siri AI preview, Siri calls only the custom intents an app marks as tools.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Count actions the metadata marks as tool intents or as adopting a schema; fail when there are none. Metadata from an SDK before 27.3 cannot mark tools, so the check is skipped and says so.
claims.fix: Mark the intents people would ask Siri for with `@AppIntent(.tool)`, building with the 27.3 SDK behind an availability check.

claims.rule: No intent is both a tool and an adopter of a schema that already reaches Siri.
claims.why: A schema in a domain Siri supports already makes the action available; marking it a tool as well is the misuse Apple's guide names.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: For each action that adopts a schema, fail when the metadata also marks it a tool and the schema's domain is one Siri reaches.
claims.fix: Remove `.tool` from that intent; the schema already brings it to Siri. Use `@AppIntent(.tool, schema:)` only for Shortcuts-only domains.

claims.rule: The app offers App Shortcuts for its main actions, so Siri and Spotlight find them with no setup.
claims.why: App Shortcuts are how an app's actions reach Siri and Spotlight before the person builds anything.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Read `autoShortcuts` in the metadata; fail when there are none.
claims.fix: Add an `AppShortcutsProvider` with an `AppShortcut` for each main action, with phrases that include the app's name.

claims.rule: When an intent is refused, its error is one sentence that says what to do next.
claims.why: Siri reads the error to the person; an error that names the fix lets the person, or Siri, recover in one step.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: With AppIntentsTesting, run each intent that takes an entity with a made-up entity reference, which nothing can match; fail when the run succeeds, or the error is empty, shows a domain and code, or names no next step.
claims.fix: Throw an error that conforms to `CustomLocalizedStringResourceConvertible` and says what to do: "There's no note X. Pick one from your notes, then try again."

claims.rule: An intent whose result other people see asks the person to confirm before it acts.
claims.why: Siri can run an intent from a misheard request; a confirmation stops a message or a share from going out by mistake.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: A person runs each intent that sends, shares or posts, through Siri and Shortcuts on a device, and checks that it asks first.
claims.fix: Call `requestConfirmation` before the intent sends, shares or posts anything other people see.

claims.rule: Each intent appears under the app in Shortcuts, and its parameter summary reads like a sentence.
claims.why: People read and edit the summary; awkward phrasing cannot be found by a code-level test.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: A person opens the Shortcuts action library on a device, finds each intent under the app's name and reads its summary.
claims.fix: Give the intent a `parameterSummary` that reads as a sentence, such as `Summary("Open \(\.$note)")`.

claims.rule: Siri calls the right intent with the right parameters for direct, indirect and incomplete wording, and declines unexpected requests.
claims.why: This is the outcome the metadata claims are for: Siri doing what the person asked.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Run the app's SiriEvaluations scenario set at least five times on a 27.3 beta OS; each scenario's `Calls` must pass at the set's threshold.
claims.fix: Read the failing transcripts and sharpen the intent's title, description, parameter descriptions or app skill.

claims.rule: After an action, what Siri says names what happened.
claims.why: The person hears the outcome, not only a chime; a reply that names the result is the spoken receipt.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: In the scenario set, `SiriResponse` expectations on each action's turn must pass.
claims.fix: Return a result with a dialog or a value that names the outcome, such as `.result(dialog: "Added milk to Groceries.")`.

claims.rule: Every entity type has a display name a person would say, not its type name.
claims.why: Siri and Shortcuts name the kind of thing with it ("Recipe", "Note").

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Read each entity's `displayTypeName` in the metadata; fail when it is empty or equals the type name.
claims.fix: Set `static let typeDisplayRepresentation: TypeDisplayRepresentation = "<a person's word for it>"`.

claims.rule: An entity exposes what a person would ask about it as properties.
claims.why: Siri matches requests to content through an entity's properties; an entity with none offers only its display text.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Read each entity's `properties` in the metadata; fail when there are none. Transient entities are skipped.
claims.fix: Add `@Property(title:)` (with `description:` on the 27.3 SDK) for each fact a person would ask about: name, date, amount.

claims.rule: Every entity property has a description.
claims.why: Siri relies on a property's description to match it to a request and to present it.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Read each property's description in the metadata; fail when it is missing. Xcode 27.2's `@Property` takes no description, so metadata from an SDK before 27.3 is skipped, and the report says so.
claims.fix: Pass `description:` to each `@Property`, `@DeferredProperty` and `@ComputedProperty`, building with the 27.3 SDK.

claims.rule: Sensitive properties require authentication, and properties only the app needs are hidden from Siri.
claims.why: By default Siri and Shortcuts can show entity information without unlocking; financial or health data should not be.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: A person reviews the report's list of each entity's properties and their authentication policy, and marks any that are sensitive or internal.
claims.fix: Pass `authenticationPolicy: .requiresAuthentication` to sensitive properties and `visibility: .internal` to app-only ones.

claims.rule: Siri can find every entity: it is indexed in Spotlight, or its query can list or search it.
claims.why: Siri finds entities through Spotlight, an enumerable query or dynamic options; an entity it cannot find, it cannot act on.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: In the metadata, pass when the entity is an `IndexedEntity`, or its default query is enumerable or answers string searches; fail otherwise.
claims.fix: Make the entity an `IndexedEntity` and index it with `CSSearchableIndex.indexAppEntities`, or give it an `EnumerableEntityQuery` or `EntityStringQuery`.

claims.rule: An entity that says it is indexed is in the Spotlight index once the app has content.
claims.why: Spotlight is the door to personal context: Siri answers from what the app indexed.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: With AppIntentsTesting, call `spotlightQuery(nil)` for each `IndexedEntity`; fail when it returns nothing while the entity's own query returns entities. Skipped when the app has no content of that type on the test device.
claims.fix: Call `CSSearchableIndex.default().indexAppEntities(_:)` when content is created or changes, and on first launch.

claims.rule: An entity's identifier resolves back to the same entity.
claims.why: Siri holds an entity by identifier between turns; one that does not resolve breaks a multi-turn request.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: With AppIntentsTesting, take the entities the query suggests and ask for them by identifier; fail when any is missing.
claims.fix: Make the query's `entities(for:)` return every identifier its other methods hand out.

claims.rule: Entities that leave the app are `Transferable`.
claims.why: Siri moves content between apps ("email this recipe"); an entity with no transferable representation cannot go anywhere.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Read each entity's `transferableContentTypes.exportableTypes` in the metadata; fail when there are none.
claims.fix: Conform the entity to `Transferable` with at least one representation other apps read, such as plain text or a file.

claims.rule: An exported entity can be read back.
claims.why: Apple names a broken Transferable as the way multi-turn Siri requests and drag and drop silently fail.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: With AppIntentsTesting, export one entity of each Transferable type and resolve it back; fail when either step throws. Skipped when the app has no content of that type.
claims.fix: Give the entity an importing representation, or a `ProxyRepresentation`, that turns the exported data back into the entity.

claims.rule: Each entity shows a title a person recognises, with a subtitle or image where it helps.
claims.why: The display representation is what the person sees in Siri, Shortcuts and Spotlight; code-level tests cannot read it.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: A person searches Spotlight and picks the entity in Shortcuts on a device, and checks the title, subtitle and image.
claims.fix: Return a `DisplayRepresentation(title:subtitle:image:)` built from the entity's own fields.

claims.rule: Siri finds the entity the person means from their words.
claims.why: Finding the right recipe or note is most of the work in a request about it.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: In the scenario set, `Finds` expectations must pass at the set's threshold.
claims.fix: Index the entity's searchable text, describe its properties, and make its display title the name people use.

claims.rule: Entities shown on screen are annotated, so "this" means what the person sees.
claims.why: Onscreen context lets a person say "add this to my list"; without an annotation Siri cannot know what "this" is.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: With AppIntentsTesting, launch the app and call `viewAnnotations()` for every entity type; pass when any is annotated. When none is, skip and say a person should open a screen that shows entities.
claims.fix: Add `.appEntityIdentifier(EntityIdentifier(for: entity))` to each row or detail view that shows an entity, or set `NSUserActivity.appEntityIdentifier` for a single one.

claims.rule: Siri resolves "this" to the entity on screen.
claims.why: The annotation is for this moment: the person points at something and asks.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: In the scenario set, `OnScreen` expectations must pass at the set's threshold.
claims.fix: Annotate the views that show entities, and keep the selected one marked as selected.

claims.rule: A skills bundle is `Skills.skillsbundle` holding only `Skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, one bundle per target.
claims.why: Siri reads nothing else in the bundle, so anything else is dead weight or a sign of a misplaced file.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Run `ouro-ax-skills lint` on each `.skillsbundle` in the app; fail on `bundle-name`, `stray-file`, `skills-folder-missing` or `skill-md-missing`.
claims.fix: Keep one `Skills.skillsbundle` per target with one folder per skill, each holding only SKILL.md.

claims.rule: Each skill's name is lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, the same in its folder and frontmatter, and unique across the app.
claims.why: When two skills share a name the system uses one of them, and which one is undefined.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Run `ouro-ax-skills lint`; fail on `skill-name`, `duplicate-name` or `name-mismatch`.
claims.fix: Rename the skill folder and its `name:` to one lowercase-hyphen name used nowhere else in the app.

claims.rule: A skill's frontmatter holds only `name` and `description`.
claims.why: App skills take a subset of the Agent Skills format; other fields are not read.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Run `ouro-ax-skills lint`; fail on `frontmatter-missing`, `frontmatter-field`, `frontmatter-duplicate`, `name-missing` or `description-missing`.
claims.fix: Start SKILL.md with `---`, `name: <folder name>`, `description: <the requests it handles>`, `---`, and nothing else.

claims.rule: A skill's body is at most 10,000 characters and names tools informally, not by type.
claims.why: Siri reads at most 10,000 characters, and knows tools by their titles, not their Swift names.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: Run `ouro-ax-skills lint`; fail on `body-too-long`, `body-empty` or `intent-type-name`.
claims.fix: Cut the body to what the intents' titles and descriptions don't already say, and call each tool by its title ("the add item tool").

claims.rule: Siri loads the skill for the requests it is written for.
claims.why: A skill Siri never loads is guidance nobody reads.

evidence.finding: No evaluation has shown Siri failing without it yet.

claims.check: In the scenario set, `Loads(.required)` expectations must pass at the set's threshold. App skills run on a device, not in Simulator.
claims.fix: Make the skill's `description` name the requests it handles, in the words people use.
